problems: Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Lithuania' row (1919-1939) is interwar Lithuania, not the Kingdom of Lithuania of the Wikipedia page it links (the 1251-1263 kingdom, with one paragraph on the 1918 monarchy); the dossier keeps the slug kingdom-of-lithuania but is the Republic of Lithuania from 16 February 1918 to July 1940; the row's display name and wikipedia field should be changed.

Shared Wikidata ids: kingdom-of-romania/romania (Q203493) and yugoslavia/socialist-federal-republic-of-yugoslavia (Q83286) are different states (a monarchy and a post-war republic with the communist period between), not merged; hungarian-republic is the Hungary of the regency and its successor slug is second-hungarian-republic (the 'hungary' dossier now starts in 1989).

Pages: 26 distinct pages were opened; per-dossier source counts add up to 33 because seven pages are cited by two or three dossiers (Axis occupation of Yugoslavia, Trianon, Hungarian-Romanian War, Vilnius Region, Invasion of Poland, Democratic Federal Yugoslavia, Second Vienna Award); Hungary lists 7, Romania, Lithuania, Poland and Yugoslavia 6 each against a budget of 5, Austria 2 against 1-2.
The URL Interwar_Lithuania redirected to a generic History of Lithuania page without a 1918-1940 section; only its 16 February 1918 sentence was used. No other page failed.
Counterpart slug central-lithuania (Poland, Lithuania) has no dossier yet and state-of-slovenes-croats-and-serbs is a predecessor slug of yugoslavia with none; the validator warns on the first.

Cliopatria year-snapshot shapes mix mid-year states (Romania 1940, Hungary 1940, Poland 1936-1938 before Trans-Olza): these are marked ok with the later within-year events carried in the ledger by month.

Poland's Upper Silesia events of 1922 are confidence 1 and take their date from the Weimar dossier because the pages opened were silent; Slovak-Hungarian War is confidence 1/2 in the Hungarian dossier (the slovak-republic dossier gives 23 March - 4 April 1939).

Dating differences with neighbours' dossiers (Transylvania 1918 vs Trianon 1920, Trans-Olza 1 vs 2 October 1938, Vilnius 10 vs 28 October 1939, Bulgarian zone in Yugoslavia as occupation vs annexation of 14 May 1941) are explained in the dossiers' notes.
